note: Adapted from Holmgren's (1913) original species-level description (published as Mirotermes (Cubitermes) zuluensis n. sp.); the original is in German and describes only the alate and a young queen, the soldier being unknown; measurements in mm, some figures damaged in the scan and not entered. Type locality East Zululand. The author notes that the species is closely related to bilobatus (printed dzlodatus in the original).

sections.label: Other
sections.text: Alate (queen): deep chestnut brown; postclypeus pale yellowish brown, antennae creamy yellow; the middle of the anterior sternites paler. Head almost hairless, the abdominal tergites with fine hairs. Head broadly oval, slightly narrowed anteriorly; compound eyes rather small, slightly projecting; ocelli medium-sized, slightly more than their own diameter from the compound eye; fontanelle distinct, punctiform, before the middle of the head, with a pale dot in front of it; on each side of the transverse band a pale transverse line and a distinct antennal spot; the middle and anterior part of the head rather strongly depressed. Postclypeus about half as long as wide, rather strongly arched, the posterior margin strongly convex and the anterior margin straight; first mandibular tooth much longer than the second; antennae 14-segmented (only 14 preserved), segment 2 longer than segments 3 and 4 together, segment 3 as long as segment 4 and segment 5 slightly longer, segments 3—5 thicker than segment 6. Pronotum large, the anterior margin slightly concave with rounded anterior corners, the posterior margin wide and distinctly notched; mesonotum and metanotum wide, the mesonotum wider than the metanotum and its notch deeper, the posterior projections of both nearly rectangular. Measurements of the young queen: body length 13.5 mm, head length 1.52 mm, head width 1.37 mm, pronotum length 0.72 mm.
